findings.passage: Republicans’ SAVE Act would strip the right to vote from those who don’t already have a passport or birth certificate, or the time and money to expedite getting one.
findings.note: Senate floor remarks, issued as an official press release. He says the SAVE Act's documentary proof-of-citizenship rule would keep people without a passport or birth certificate from voting.

findings.passage: It is today’s poll tax...This is not a voter ID bill. This is a voter suppression bill.
findings.note: Same floor remarks. He describes the SAVE Act's costs and document rules as a poll tax and rejects calling it a voter ID bill. He also names effects on mail registration and mail voting.

findings.passage: I call upon my colleagues in the Senate: Choose freedom. Choose democracy. And say ‘no’ to the so-called SAVE Act.
findings.note: He closes his Senate floor remarks by asking colleagues to vote no on the SAVE Act. The same release says he also described his work on foreign interference, election security funding in New Mexico, election certification, and the John R. Lewis Voting Rights Act.

findings.passage: I believe in having a way to verify citizenship – but a Jim Crow 2.0 is not it.
findings.note: Signed newsletter-style post on his official site. He says he supports a way to verify citizenship but opposes the SAVE Act's approach. The post is titled 'It's not a voter ID bill – it's voter suppression.'

findings.passage: “Requiring voters to purchase or renew a passport for $130 is a modern day poll tax. This is Jim Crow 2.0,” he said.
findings.note: Quoted by KUNM (reposted on his official site) from his Senate floor remarks. He objects to the passport cost as a way to meet proof of citizenship.

findings.passage: “This legislation would be absolutely devastating for New Mexicans,” Heinrich said during a roundtable on elections at the Santa Fe Community College.
findings.note: Quoted by the Santa Fe New Mexican (reposted on his official site) at a roundtable on the SAVE Act's proof-of-citizenship and photo ID rules. The article also quotes him: "Our message today is simple: Not on our watch."

findings.passage: “His Department of Justice is literally suing Secretary Toulouse Oliver to gain access to full, unredacted statewide voter registration records. Those are your records, your Social Security numbers.”
findings.note: Related topic, voter-roll data. He objects to a federal demand for New Mexico's full voter registration records. Quoted by the Santa Fe New Mexican; the paper's text begins the quote with 'When he [Trump] isn't trying to dismantle our local elections, he is trying to get his hands on your personal information,' Heinrich said.

Press release says Heinrich and another senator introduced S.1, the For the People Act. The release says the bill would, among other things, ensure that discriminatory voter ID laws do not prevent American citizens from voting, ban voter roll purges, expand voting by mail, and fund election security upgrades. Passage quoted from the release: 'ensuring that discriminatory voter ID laws do not prevent Americans citizens from exercising their rights.'

findings.motion: Senate roll call 57, motion to proceed to S. 1383 (the legislative vehicle for the House-passed SAVE America Act); agreed to 51-48
findings.note: Heinrich is on the nay list. The SAVE America Act would require documentary proof of citizenship to register for federal elections and photo ID to vote, per the Ballotpedia explainer https://news.ballotpedia.org/2026/03/25/senate-takes-up-save-america-act-to-require-voter-id-proof-of-citizenship-for-federal-elections/. The tracking site labels S. 1383 with an unrelated title because the Senate used that bill number as the vehicle; the Senate Press Gallery log calls it the legislative vehicle for the SAVE Act. Official senate.gov roll call page could not be fetched.
subjects: photo ID to vote in federal elections

findings.motion: Senate roll call 73, cloture on S.Amdt. 4732 to S.Amdt. 4420 to S. 1383, an amendment 'to require voters to provide photo identification'; cloture not invoked, 53-47
findings.note: Heinrich is on the nay list for cloture on the Husted photo-ID amendment. The Senate Press Gallery log for the day (https://www.dailypress.senate.gov/thursday-march-26-2026/) describes it as cloture on the Husted amendment #4732 in relation to the House message to accompany S.1383.
subjects: photo ID to vote in federal elections

findings.passage: “Requiring voters to purchase or renew a passport for $130 is a modern day poll tax. This is Jim Crow 2.0,” he said.
findings.note: Quoted by KUNM from his Senate floor remarks of 2026-03-18 on the SAVE Act's proof-of-citizenship documents. The same story reports, in the reporter's words, that Heinrich said it is not a voter ID bill but a voter suppression bill.

findings.passage: “All American citizens should have the same right to vote as the senators in this room, all American citizens deserve to hold the reins of this great democracy in their hands. So for those constituents, for all Americans, I say again, either we are all free or we fail,” he said.
findings.note: Closing lines of his Senate floor remarks on the SAVE Act, as quoted by KUNM.

findings.passage: “This legislation would be absolutely devastating for New Mexico,” said Heinrich. “Now I don’t need to tell you how many New Mexicans do not have a passport.”
findings.note: Quoted by KOB at a New Mexico state-leaders event on the SAVE Act's proof-of-citizenship requirement (story published 2026-02-28 UTC).
